Brand details · v1.0
UNBC's Independent Student Newspaper

Drawn in the margins.

The full reference for Over the Edge's "Doodle" identity: the paper's own lettering in Cream, Forest, Lichen and Ink, Decalotype headlines, Helvetica Neue for reading, Salted for the handwritten accents, and the line doodles students leave in their notebooks. Everything here is drawn from one brand.json.

v1.0overtheedge.unbc.caGenerated by brandkit
Positioning and voice

Students talking to students.

Curious, warm and a little wry. Plain in the news; playful in features, when the story earns it.

Breaking news, vibrant clubs, can’t-miss events, and a shared university calendar.
The paper's own line, from its homepage
  • HeadlinesTitle Case, as the site and the covers set them: “Bears Don’t Really Hibernate… Or Do They?”, “Green So Far”.
  • First personWelcome in features and columns. Never in news.
  • Exclamation marksFeatures and event promotion only.
  • DatesMonth spelled out: “[Mon] [D], [YYYY]” on screen, “[MONTH] [D]TH” on covers. Never all numbers, which readers split on.
  • EmojiNone in headlines, navigation or interface.
Logo

The paper’s own lettering.

Drawn path for path from the SVG the site serves. One colour at a time: Forest on Cream or Lichen, Lichen on Ink, Cream on Forest.

  • Clear spaceHalf the height of the O on every side.
  • NeverRedraw it, reset it in a font, outline it, stretch it, add effects, or set it in two colours other than the site's original (kept in logos/source/).
Colour

Cream, Forest, Lichen, Ink.

The identity's four colours, read from its own files' fills, then four tints sampled from its posts. The earlier Forest press colours follow, kept for the supporting studies and the site.

  • Forest#155329The brand. The logo, headlines, photo blocks, day tags and stickers.
  • Cream#FFFBF3The page. Most posts, stories and slides start here.
  • Lichen#E3EFCFThe second ground; the logo and text on Forest or Ink; the doodle wall.
  • Ink#262626Body text, Salted accents and doodles on light grounds; a dark ground for season posts.
  • Haze#F5F1EAOVER THE EDGE repeated faintly behind a schedule on Cream. Never text.
  • Flame#FFF2D8The big flame behind a deadline on Cream. Never text.
  • Crumple#F4F4F4The crumpled sheet a schedule is printed on.
  • Ember#6D4900The issue number on the Cream deadline post.
  • White#FFFFFFHighlights in crumpled paper; text on Forest where Cream is not to hand.
  • Pine#0C3B1CEarlier Forest press colour, kept for the supporting studies.
  • Sage#6AA380Earlier Forest press colour: large figures on Forest, 24 px and up.
  • Moss#466855Earlier Forest press colour: the photo well of the issue cover.
  • Kraft#D4C8AAEarlier Forest press colour: rules and placeholders only.
  • Pulp#DBD0BAEarlier Forest press colour: hairlines and quiet patterns only.
  • Bark#7D6B56Earlier Forest press colour: labels on the cards and letterhead.
  • Proof#B54A35Earlier Forest press colour: Breaking and Correction, and nothing else.

Typography

Three voices.

The identity names Decalotype, Helvetica Neue and Salted. Decalotype is a commercial face, so Anton stands in for it. Helvetica Neue and Salted are supplied originals; keep their notices.

Headlines · Decalotype (Anton)Submission Schedule
Reading · Helvetica NeueOver the Edge is a student-run newspaper and creative platform that gives students space to share their voices, perspectives, and ideas.

Doodles and templates

Drawn in the margins.

Googly eyes, a calendar with a clock, a flame, a pencil, a paper plane and a spark, at one round stroke. Around them: dashed rules, tilted day tags, blob stickers, crumpled paper and a faint OVER THE EDGE ground. The Staff Card is the press pass.

Motion

Off the press, one word at a time.

The full library, with replay, is motion/index.html in the kit and brandkit's Motion tab.

  • PressLogo

    OVER, THE and EDGE print in one at a time, dropping a few pixels into place; then UNBC’S STUDENT NEWSPAPER rises under them.

  • StackLogo

    The stacked logo, each line rising out of its own mask, as on the October 2025 cover.

  • InkLogo

    The logo is uncovered left to right, the way a roller lays ink on a plate.

  • Rolling rulesLoading

    The issue index’s dashed rules roll past, one line after another.

  • Page countLoading

    Anton page numbers turn over: 03, 05, 10, as in the index.

  • O fillLoading

    The O fills with forest from the foot up, holds, and empties. The O only; it stops when loading ends.

  • Paper airplaneLoading

    A paper airplane, like the one drawn on the October 2025 cover, glides along a dashed line.

  • HeadlineInterface

    Each line of an Anton headline rises out of its own mask.

  • Card pickInterface

    A story card lifts 3 px, shifts 1 px and turns 0.4°, like a clipping picked up off the desk, then settles.

  • IndexInterface

    Each dashed rule draws across, then its page number and headline come in.

  • ChipInterface

    A filter chip presses in to 96%, and its border and label turn forest.

  • Turn pageInterface

    The next page slides over from the right edge, square-cornered, like turning a broadsheet.

  • SkeletonInterface

    Placeholder lines in Pulp with a Newsprint highlight passing along them.

Where it can go next

Ideas the system makes easy. None of them is decided.
